subject: Discovery recap: EnterpriseMeds - Private/VPC deployment requirements
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.in>
To: Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@enterprisemeds.com>
Cc: James O'Neil <j.oneil@enterprisemeds.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Feb 2026 16:10:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery recap: EnterpriseMeds - Private/VPC deployment requirements

Hi Priya / James,

Thanks again for the time today — appreciate the clear overview of your use case and constraints. Below is a quick recap from our call so we have alignment and clear next steps. Please correct anything I missed.

Summary of pain & goals
- Regulated clinical data (PHI) must remain inside EnterpriseMeds network and meet HIPAA controls.
- Current generation models run inference against patient records for triage and summarization; latency requirement is ~150ms P95 for single-session lookups.
- Primary goal: run Redwood inference behind your VPC or on-prem so you control networking, key management, and audit logs.

Current stack & constraints
- AWS (us-east-1) account, VPC with strict egress rules, existing VPC peering with a shared services VPC.
- We cannot allow outbound traffic to Redwood-hosted endpoints; everything must be routed privately or run on-prem.
- They require customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for model artifacts and logs.
- A potential air-gap requirement for offline sites (non-prod PoC first).

Success criteria for POC
- Deploy Redwood Private in a customer-managed VPC (or on-prem appliance) with VPC peering and no public egress.
- Demonstrate model serving with P95 latency <= 200ms on representative test workload.
- Show encryption-at-rest with CMEK (customer-managed keys) and audit log access for compliance team.

Risks / open items
- Network setup: need details on proxy/NAT constraints and whether cross-account IAM roles are acceptable.
- HSM integration: which vendor (AWS CloudHSM vs. external) and rotation policies.
- Air-gapped sites: scope and timeline—may require offline installer and manual package installs.

Next steps (owners & timing)
- EnterpriseMeds: share network diagram, egress rules, and preferred KMS/HSM vendor by Tue, Mar 3 — Priya (owner).
- Redwood: provide Private deployment checklist and SOC2 attestation redacted copy by Mon, Mar 2 — Marissa (owner).
- Schedule technical deep-dive with solutions engineer to review VPC peering and key integration — propose Wed, Mar 4 (Dylan to lead).

Attachments: redwood-private-deployment-checklist.pdf (deployment checklist), SOC2_attestation_redacted.pdf (for compliance).

Thanks — I look forward to the next steps.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@enterprisemeds.com>

Date: Sun, 1 Mar 2026 09:35:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: EnterpriseMeds - Private/VPC deployment requirements

Marissa — thanks for the thorough recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- Network: we use centralized NAT in the shared-services VPC today; we prefer either VPC peering or AWS PrivateLink if that reduces blast radius. No outbound public IPs allowed from the subnets that will host inference.
- KMS/HSM: primary preference is AWS CloudHSM; our security team may require an HSM-backed KEK. We will confirm exact rotation policy.
- Latency: 150ms P95 is ideal but for the POC we can accept up to 200ms; production target is 150ms.
- Air-gap: one regional clinical site has an air-gapped environment; we will need an offline package and manual install process for non-prod validation.

We’ll pull together the network diagram and a short doc on HSM requirements and share by Tue, Mar 3 as requested.

Thanks — Priya
Priya Sharma

EnterpriseMeds

Great — thanks Priya. I’m looping in Dylan (solutions engineering) to coordinate the technical deep-dive and validate the checklist items that will affect the install path.

Dylan — quick note on what to prepare for Wed:
- VPC peering vs PrivateLink implications (routing, transitive access, cross-account role setup).
- CloudHSM integration options and whether Redwood Private can be configured to use customer KMS/HSM for secrets and model keys.
- Offline installer flow for air-gapped site (what artifacts we need to provide, approximate time to install).

I’ll upload the checklist and SOC2 pdf to the shared folder; attaching here for your reference.

Marissa

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.in>
To: Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@enterprisemeds.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.in>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 10:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: EnterpriseMeds - Private/VPC deployment requirements

Hi Priya / Marissa — quick technical notes ahead of Wed’s deep-dive: 

1) VPC connectivity options
- VPC Peering: simplest for us, low latency; requires route table updates and cross-account peering. No transitive peering so we need to ensure shared-services access is considered.
- PrivateLink: slightly more setup but reduces need for cross-account IAM trusts; can be used if NAT rules are restrictive.

2) KMS/HSM
- We support using customer KMS for encrypting configuration and artifacts; for HSM-backed KEKs we will need details on key wrapping and whether CloudHSM is used via AWS KMS or a dedicated on-prem HSM. We can support CloudHSM via an integration pattern (details in deep-dive).

3) Air-gapped installs
- We provide an offline installer package (tarball) and an installation guide. The package includes model artifacts, runtime container images (signed), and a scripted installer. Acceptance tests run locally to validate connectivity and latency. Note: for air-gap we request a 1-2 week window to stage signed artifacts and provide restart instructions.

Please send the network diagram and HSM details when available. I’ll prepare a short runbook for the deep-dive (VPC diagrams, port list, preflight checks).

Thanks,
